<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par113 />absolute is most frequently used in this way, corresponding to the infinitive of command in Greek, &c.<ref>Cf. also such infinitives in French as ''voir'' (page so and so, &c.), ''s’adresser..., se méfier des voleurs''!</ref>:—

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|bb}}
(α) For an emphatic imperative,<ref>Prätorius, ''op. cit.'', p. 547: the extraordinarily common use of the infinitive form ''qāṭōl'' in the sense of an imperative, jussive, or cohortative has long since caused it to be compared with the Arab. ''faʿāli''. It thus appears that the infin. ''qāṭōl'' in Hebrew could be used from early times as a kind of fixed, invariable word of command.</ref> e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמוֹר}} (thou shalt, ye shall), ''observe'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=זָכוֹר}} (thou shalt) ''remember'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=8|hidebook=1}} (the full form occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=6|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמוֹר תִּשְׁמְרוּן}}; 7:18 {{GHGheb|text=זָכֹר תִּזְכֹּר}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=2|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=4|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=25|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=2}}, followed by a {{GHGterm|perfect consecutive}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=1|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=3|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=31|hidebook=1}} (parallel with an {{GHGterm|imperative}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=2}} three imperatives follow). But {{GHGheb|text=הַבֵּיט}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=142|verse=5}} may be only an incorrect spelling of {{GHGheb|text=הַבֵּט}} imperative.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=31}}, for the infinitives construct {{GHGheb|text=הָסִיר}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָרִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַשְׁפִּיל}} (beside {{GHGheb|text=הַגְבֵּהַּ}}) read with Cornill the infinitives absolute {{GHGheb|text=הָסֵר}}, &c. The K<sup>e</sup>thîbh probably intends {{GHGheb|text=הָסֵיר}}, &c.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|cc}}
(β) For the jussive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=6|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=6|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=46}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=17|verse=12}} (''let it'' rather ''meet'').

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|dd}}
(γ) For the cohortative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=13}}b {{GHGheb|text=אָכוֹל וְשָׁתוֹ}} (the exclamation of the mocker); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=30|hidebook=1}}, 46; perhaps also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=2}} ({{GHGheb|text=הָלוֹךְ}}).<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=18}} the infinitive construct appears to be used instead of the cohortative, but {{GHGheb|text=אוֹשִׁיעַ}} should certainly be read for {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשִׁיעַ}}. Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=30}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=18|verse=29}}), which was formerly included under this head (I will ''disguise myself and go into the battle''), read {{GHGheb|text=אֶתְחַפֵּשׂ וְאָבֹא}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|ee}}
(δ) For the imperfect in emphatic promises, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=43}} ye shall ''eat and leave thereof''; 19:29 ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=30}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=31|verse=10}}; also in indignant questions, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=2}} ''shall he that cavilleth contend with the Almighty?''<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=18}} in a similar question instead of the infinitive constr. we should rather expect the infinitive absolute ({{GHGheb|text=הֶאָמֹר}}), unless with the LXX and Vulg. the participle with the article ({{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֹמֵר}}) is to be read.</ref> (on the addition of the subject cf. the Rem. below); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=1}} ''and thinkest thou to return again to me?'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=9}} ff. (six infinitives, continued by means of the {{GHGterm|perfect consecutive}}; cf. {{GHGpar|112|o}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|ff}}
(ε) For any historical tense (like the Latin ''historic'' infinitive) in lively narration (or enumeration) and description, even of what is still taking place in present time, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hos|chapter=4|verse=2}} ''swearing and breaking faith, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery'' (in these they are busied); 10:4 (after a {{GHGterm|perfect}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=14|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=35}}; cf. further {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=2}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=12|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=15|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, and 25:4, the infinitive absolute is best rendered by the passive.<section end=par113 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
